title: Overlapping bookings under concurrency
idea: A double booking happens when two requests both see a room free and both add a booking; the fix makes check and insert atomic per room.

analogy.text: Two colleagues both see 10:30 free on the door sheet and both sign. A pen chained to the door: only the pen holder may read the sheet and write.
analogy.breaks: The pen is per room; other rooms keep their own pens.

points: Overlap is a range question, so `putIfAbsent` on one key cannot answer it.
A lock per room serializes check and insert; different rooms run in parallel.
No-shows are released by a sweeper that receives the current time as input.
When v2 adds recurring series, book them all or nothing.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. Asha checks whether 10:00-11:00 is free in R-1.
Before Asha writes, Ravi checks 10:30-11:30. The calendar is still empty.
Both threads now hold yes. Neither knows the other exists.
Both add their booking. The room now has two overlapping meetings.
Locked version. Asha takes the lock for R-1 first.
Under the lock Asha checks and adds. Ravi waits at the lock.
Asha releases the lock. Ravi takes it and checks against the updated calendar.
10:30 overlaps Asha's meeting, so Ravi gets a conflict. One winner.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier makes both threads look before either writes, so the race shows up on every run.

walk.text: Run the same two requests twice: unsafe first, then with a room lock.
Two threads book overlapping slots in R-1; join both before reading wins.
The overlap rule on minutes: each starts before the other ends.
Unsafe: check, wait at the barrier, then write. The write is synchronized; the pair is not.
`computeIfAbsent` creates exactly one lock per room, even under races.
Check and insert run under that lock, so the second thread sees the first booking.

code.title: No-shows and series
code.caption: Time is passed in, so the no-show sweeper and the series check replay the same way every run.

walk.text: Back-to-back bookings both succeed: the intervals are half-open.
Sweep at 10:05 and 10:12; then a walk-in tries the freed slot.
A v2 preview: a three-day series at 11:30, booked all or nothing.
Release a booking when it is not checked in after its grace period.
Check every occurrence first; insert only when none clashes.

pitfalls: Never check `isFree` and add in separate steps without one lock around both.
One global lock is correct but slow; lock per room, not per service.
In v2, never insert a series occurrence by occurrence; a later clash leaves a partial series.

quiz.q: What does the series line of EdgeCases print?
quiz.why: Today's 11:30-12:30 overlaps BK-2 from 11:00 to 12:00. The first clash stops the series before any occurrence is inserted.

takeaway: Check overlap and insert under one lock per room.

starters: Why can a ConcurrentHashMap alone not prevent overlapping bookings?
How does this lock work when the service runs on three servers?
Should a series with one clash be refused or booked partly?
